title: Platform dashboards, alerts, and runbook - playbook + retrospective + roadmap
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This playbook consolidates the platform team’s canonical dashboards, alerting rules, on-call runbooks, retrospective findings, and short-term roadmap for dashboards & alerts. It is intended as the single reference for on-call engineers, SREs, and platform owners when investigating service degradations and planning monitoring improvements.
body:
Overview:
This document groups: 1) current production dashboards (Grafana) and their intent, 2) Prometheus/Alertmanager rules and severity, 3) step-by-step runbooks for the top 6 alert classes, 4) escalation policy and runbook ownership, 5) retrospective findings from Q4 2025 incidents related to observability, and 6) roadmap items for Q1–Q2 2026.

Organization and intent:
- Audience: platform engineers, on-call SREs, platform product owners, and incident commanders.
- Ownership: observability stack is owned by Platform::Observability + Eng-SRE as primary responders.
- Tooling: Grafana (dashboards), Prometheus (metrics), Alertmanager (routing), PagerDuty (escalation), CloudWatch (supplemental logs), Datadog traces for distributed traces.

How to use this page:
1) For any alert, open the alert-runbook below that matches the alert name.
2) Use the linked Grafana dashboard for triage.
3) If mitigation is required, follow the mitigation steps and notify stakeholders via the incident channel.

Documentation style note: dashboards and rules below list canonical panel IDs and query hints (not full source).
slos: API availability (hosted API): 99.95% monthly uptime (SLO owner: eng-sre)
99th percentile token latency for open models: <= 450ms P99 (measured at ingress queue; SLO owner: eng-serving-runtime)
Request error rate for generation endpoints: <= 0.5% (5xx+timeout) over 10m rolling window
Model-serving throughput SLO: maintain 95% of committed RPS for Dedicated clusters under normal load patterns
dashboards: Grafana - Platform Overview (dashboard id: platform-overview): traffic, error rate, P50/P95/P99 latencies for generation, embeddings, and reranking routes. Use when first triaging system-wide alerts.

Grafana - Model Serving Health (dashboard id: model-serving-health): per-pool GPU utilization, queue length, KV cache hit ratio, and OOM events. Panels: gpu_utilization, queue_depth_by_pool, kv_cache_hit_rate.

Grafana - Ingress & Routing (dashboard id: ingress-routing): request distribution by region, route-level latency heatmap, cache hit ratio by route. Useful for diagnosing routing fallbacks and regional degradations.
Grafana - Autoscaler & Capacity (dashboard id: autoscaler-capacity): pending pods/agents, scale-up events, failed scale attempts. Correlate with capacity alerts to determine scaling failures.
Grafana - Platform Errors (dashboard id: platform-errors): grouped 5xx by service, top callstacks, recent deployment overlays. Helpful for root-cause during release-related incidents.
Grafana - Cost & Efficiency (dashboard id: cost-efficiency): token throughput vs GPU-hours, batching efficiency, and KV cache savings. Used in post-incident cost analysis and optimization planning.
alerting_rules: PLATFORM_HIGH_ERROR_RATE (severity: critical): service-wide 5xx rate > 1.5% sustained over 5m OR route-level 5xx > 3% over 5m. Route to P1 escalation. Runbook: triage service logs, identify recent deploy, rollback if needed.

MODEL_P99_LATENCY_HIGH (severity: high): P99 latency for generation endpoints > 750ms over 5m. Investigate queue depth, GPU saturation, and KV cache hit rate. If due to sustained saturation, trigger scale-up and notify product owners.

QUEUE_BACKPRESSURE_ALERT (severity: high): ingress queue length per pool > 750 for 3m OR average wait_time > 200ms. Mitigation: enable burst capacity policy, throttle low-priority routes, or fail-fast non-essential routes.
GPU_OOM_RATE_INCREASE (severity: high): OOM events per GPU > 2 in 10m. Mitigation: mark node pool as tainted, decrease concurrency, schedule rolling redeploy of pods with adjusted memory flags.

AUTOSCALER_FAILURE (severity: critical): failed scale-up attempts > 2 within 10m OR provisioner API errors. Mitigation: inspect cloud quota, provisioner logs, and fallback to Dedicated burst pool if available.

KV_CACHE_DEGRADATION (severity: medium): KV cache hit rate drop > 25% vs baseline for 10m. Investigate cache eviction patterns and model version mismatches. Consider warming cache and rolling model variant fallback.
runbook_steps: 1) PLATFORM_HIGH_ERROR_RATE: (a) Open platform-errors Grafana, filter to last 10m and the affected service. (b) Check recent deploys (CI/CD -> release-notes). (c) Capture top 5 error traces from distributed trace system. (d) If errors correlate with a deploy, initiate rollback (see deploy rollback runbook). (e) If not deploy-related, bisect by route to isolate downstream dependency and engage owner. (f) PagerDuty: trigger P1 and follow escalation_policy below.

2) MODEL_P99_LATENCY_HIGH: (a) Open model-serving-health and ingress-routing dashboards. (b) Check queue_depth_by_pool and gpu_utilization. (c) If GPU utilization > 90% for > 5m, scale up or enable burst pool. (d) If queue depth high but GPUs underutilized, check scheduler backpressure and per-request batching parameters. (e) If due to a single model version, route to model-onboarding for rollback or throttling.

3) QUEUE_BACKPRESSURE_ALERT: (a) Identify top contributing routes. (b) Apply temporary throttles on non-critical routes via rate-limiter service: curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.internal/rl/patch -d '{"routes": ["/debug"] ,"limit":100}'. (c) Enable burst capacity if configured. (d) Notify product owners and prepare follow-up to adjust routable capacity or caching.

4) GPU_OOM_RATE_INCREASE: (a) Mark nodes and cordon pool to avoid further scheduling. kubectl annotate node <node> observability/oom=true. (b) Reduce model concurrency parameter on the pool and redeploy model-serving pods. (c) If repeated OOMs, add memory safety margins to the serving config and open an RFC with runtime owners.

5) AUTOSCALER_FAILURE: (a) Check autoscaler logs in the autoscaler-capacity dashboard. (b) Verify cloud provider quota and error messages. (c) If quota exhausted, request temporary increase via cloud-accounts-and-networking process and failover to Dedicated burst capacity. (d) Post-incident: add alert to detect quota exhaustion earlier and include runbook link.

6) KV_CACHE_DEGRADATION: (a) Check kv_cache_hit_rate panel and recent evictions. (b) If model version mismatch, instruct model-onboarding to rewarm cache: run cache-sync job: /ops/cache_sync --model <model> --ttl 24h. (c) Consider adjusting cache sizing or eviction policy and schedule a follow-up evaluation.
escalation_policy: PagerDuty schedule: Primary on-call (Platform SRE) for first 15 minutes, if not acknowledged escalate to Secondary (Platform on-call) for next 15 minutes, then to Engineering Director on-call. For P1 incidents, simultaneously page Engineering Manager and Product Owner.

Contact matrix: use Slack channel #incidents-platform for ongoing comms. Post incident status updates every 30 minutes until stabilized. Use incident template in incident-process runbook for initial post.
mitigation_playbooks: Traffic spikes: enable ingress rate limiting for non-essential routes, increase batching timeout for long-running requests by 50ms to improve throughput, enable prefix caching for hot prompts.
Model regressions causing elevated errors: mark model version as 'quarantine' and switch default route to previous stable variant. Notify model-onboarding and apply code tag for rollback in CI/CD.
Capacity starved hosts: temporarily drain low-priority jobs, enable burst Dedicated pool, and launch emergency scale-up job with operator script: /ops/emergency_scale --pool <pool> --count 5.
Partial region outage: fail over traffic to nearest healthy region via smart-routing policy and set circuit-breaker for affected region to 5% of normal traffic until recovery confirmed.
postmortem_guidance: Immediate: capture timeline (UTC), initial detection method, responders, mitigation steps, and customer-impact metric (affected requests, downtime).
Root cause analysis: link to traces, top error stacks, and relevant deploy IDs. Identify contributing factors across people/process/tech.
Action items: create actionable, owner-assigned items with deadlines. Track in JIRA with label obs-incident and include this document as linked evidence.
Communication: write a short internal summary within 48 hours and a customer-facing summary where impacted customers are known.
retrospective_findings: Q4 2025 incident themes: 1) insufficient autoscaler visibility for cloud quota exhaustion, 2) unpredictable OOMs for a small set of large models, 3) delayed cache warming after rollouts causing transient latency spikes.
Completed actions: added autoscaler errors to platform-overview dashboard, implemented pre-deploy cache warm step for major model rollouts, added memory guardrails to model-serving runtime defaults.
Open items: improve alert runbook coverage for dependent services, add chaos testing for scale-up scenarios, and automate throttling for low-priority routes during overload.
roadmap_items: Q1 2026: Grafana migration - consolidate three legacy dashboards into "platform-overview" and reduce dashboard duplication (owner: Marco Alvarez, status: in_progress).
Q1 2026: Implement predictive autoscaler health check to detect quota exhaustion and pre-warm Dedicated pools (owner: Jenna Lee, status: planned).
Q2 2026: On-call tooling - add one-click rollback link in dashboards to CI/CD and surface recent deploys inline (owner: Priya Nair, status: planned).
Q2 2026: Batching efficiency panel - add per-model batching success rate and cost-savings estimator to cost-efficiency dashboard (owner: Aisha Patel, status: planned).
references: PagerDuty escalation guide: internal docs (PagerDuty schedule ID: platform-oncall-2026)
